text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- CHRISTMAS: WHOEVER SELLS MIGHT NOT RECEIVE

Sales are expected to rise only shortly before Christmas. But the Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP) warns that "whoever sells well this Christmas faces the risk of not receiving (the money)", recommending caution to retailers at year's end because of the threat of consumer defaults.

Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles on Tuesday will submit to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso a more optimistic forecast for investment in the Brazilian industry by 2000. According to the ministry, investment will rise to $94 billion from the $63 billion previously estimated between now and the year 2000.
-- NOW IT IS OFFICIAL: GM WILL INVEST $1.2 BLN
General Motors will invest $1.25 billion in new plants in three Brazilian states. Southern state of Rio Grande do Sul will have its first car plant, which will produce 100,000 passenger cars.
-- GOV'T STUDIES OFFERING MORE CVRD SHARES TO THE PUBLIC

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso agreed to study a proposal to offer more shares of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce to the public. Under Vale's sell-off plan, an initial sale of 40-45 percent block of voting shares in the company would begin in February.
-- CEF TO GRANT MORE HOUSING FUNDS
Federal bank Caixa Economica Federal will grant a further 500 million reais to finance real estate purchases.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
